messages.subject: UGP and UFL files?
parts:
Hi,
We have been using aroma.affymetrix to do 500K snp chip analysis over
the last couple of months, and we just saw the message on Feb 21st on
the website that you now recommend UGP and UFL annotation files
instead of dChip SNP and genome information.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis
"Comment on 2008-02-21: With the introduction of UGP and UFL
annotation files, we are now moving away from the dChip SNP and genome
information files previously used. The latter files should still work,
but we now recommend to use the UGP and UFL files instead."

I am wondering how much difference it will cause if we still use the
dChip SNP+genome information files as the annotation files? If we have
been using these old annotation file to do the analysis, do we need to
re-do the whole process again? Thanks!

Best regards,


Yang

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] UGP and UFL files?
parts:
Hi,

short answer: I have not made an explicit comparison, but most likely
it will not make any difference to your biological findings.

Long answer: I don't know the *exact* details on how dChip annotation
files (SNP information file and genome information file) were
generated. However, from http://www.dchip.org/ one can read that the
source for its files are the Affymetrix NetAffx CSV files (aka
"annotation CSV files"). These are also the ones used to create the
UGP and UFL files (all details on the aroma.affymetrix web site).

So, with everything else the same, it comes down to what version of
NetAffx was used. From now on the UGP and UFL files will have a tag
specifying what version of NetAffx was used and also a tag indicating
who and when that person created the file, e.g.
'Mapping250K_Nsp,na24,HB20080214.ugp' will tell you that NetAffx
release/version 24 (tag 'na24') and that user 'HB' (me) created the
file on 2008-02-14. dChip "tags" the annotation files with the genome
build instead, e.g. 'hg18'. In other words, it is a bit ambiguous
what NetAffx version dChip use, but my best guess is that Cheng Li
updates the annotation files quarterly when NetAffx get updated.

In summary, my best guess is that any differences are only minor and
won't affect your results significantly.

/Henrik

(1) The information posted here stating that frangement length effect
would be canceled out when computing log2 ratio of two samples. Does
that mean fragment length calibration makes no difference when what I
need is log2 ratio of each sample to a reference?
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calibration-and-normalization-of-summarized-data

(2) also from the same link as above, what is the current system to
track enzymes for each fragment?

(3) How the GC content of PCR fragment is calculated by
aroma.affymetrix? From what I understood, only length, start and stop
positions are required in UFL file.

(4) I have custom array thus I have to populate my own UFL file. I can
creat an annotation file similar (but not identical) to NetAffx CSV
annotation files. The questions are what the columns and column-
headers required by aroma.affymetrix?

Thanks,

Jin

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: UGP and UFL files?
parts: Hi.

On Mon, Apr 7, 2008 at 11:48 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
> Hi, Henrik, I have a couple of questions regarding to Fragment length
> calibration.
>
> (1) The information posted here stating that frangement length effect
> would be canceled out when computing log2 ratio of two samples. Does
> that mean fragment length calibration makes no difference when what I
> need is log2 ratio of each sample to a reference?
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/calibration-and-normalization-of-summarized-data

Where is "here"?

I'm not sure what your question is since you are referring to the page
explaining that we model and correct for the effect on the log2 chip
effect scale (to avoid doing it on log2 ratios which wouldn't allow us
to go back to chip effects afterward). Fragment-length effects do not
cancel out if they differ between arrays.

>
> (2) also from the same link as above, what is the current system to
> track enzymes for each fragment?

Could you please be more precise. The fragment lengths in the UFL
files are inferred from NetAffx files provided by Affymetrix.

>
> (3) How the GC content of PCR fragment is calculated by
> aroma.affymetrix? From what I understood, only length, start and stop
> positions are required in UFL file.

GC contents is not corrected for in the PCR fragment-length
normalization. The latter uses the UFL file, which as you say, do not
contain GC-content information.

There is a GcContentNormalization class normalizing CnChipEffectSet:s, e.g.

gcn <- GcContentNormalization(ces)
process(gcn, verbose=verbose)

I hardly never do GC-content normalization which is why I haven't
pushed the method nor added major support for the method. In order
process the above, you will have to download an Affymetrix TSV file
and place it in the corresponding chip-type annotationData/ directory.
You know you have it working when you can do:

> cdf <- getCdf(ces);
> tsv <- AffymetrixTsvFile$byChipType(getChipType(cdf, fullname=FALSE));
> print(tsv);
AffymetrixTsvFile:
Name: Mapping250K_Sty
Tags:
Pathname: annotationData/chipTypes/Mapping250K_Sty/Mapping250K_Sty.tsv
File size: 9.21MB
RAM: 0.00MB

That is the same code that process(gcn) use.

The Affymetrix TSV file I once got from Affymetrix (cannot remember
where), are ASCII files and are/were used by CNAT v4. They look like:


> bfr <- readLines(getPathname(tsv), n=5)
[1] "probeset_id\tchr\tsnp_pos\tlen\tGC\tgc_count"
[2] "SNP_A-1780271\t15\t31183071\t625\t35.68\t223"
[3] "SNP_A-1780274\t20\t33371323\t367\t44.959\t165"
[4] "SNP_A-1780277\t12\t73950313\t652\t41.411\t270"
[5] "SNP_A-1780278\t1\t215279053\t682\t35.924\t245"

> cat(bfr, sep="\n")
probeset_id chr snp_pos len GC gc_count
SNP_A-1780271 15 31183071 625 35.68 223
SNP_A-1780274 20 33371323 367 44.959 165
SNP_A-1780277 12 73950313 652 41.411 270
SNP_A-1780278 1 215279053 682 35.924 245

>
> (4) I have custom array thus I have to populate my own UFL file. I can
> creat an annotation file similar (but not identical) to NetAffx CSV
> annotation files. The questions are what the columns and column-
> headers required by aroma.affymetrix?

If you already have the data in a convenient data structure in R, it
might be easier for you to just allocated an empty UFL file and
populate it manually:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("Mapping250K_Nsp")
ufl <- AromaUflFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="na24,JP20080408");

The units (rows) of a UFL are ordered exactly as in the CDF. So you
have to identify the correct unit index for each unit name, e.g.

> unitNames <- c("SNP_A-1796078", "SNP_A-4250778");
> units <- indexOf(cdf, names=unitNames);
> print(units);
[1] 101 567

Then you can populate it with fragment lengths, e.g.

ufl[units,1] <- c(658, 439)


If you want to proceed by immitating a NetAffx, please see the
following source code:

print(readDataUnitFragmentLength.AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile)

/Henrik
